gaps.sentence: She ___ the world record for the 100 metres last year.
gaps.explanation: break a record is the fixed collocation for performing better than the record.

gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: Despite the pressure, the surgeon ___ calm throughout the operation.
gaps.explanation: keep calm (or stay calm) means to remain calm; the past tense is needed here.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a fortune by buying his train ticket in advance.
gaps.explanation: save a fortune means to avoid spending a large amount; buying in advance keeps money.

gaps.sentence: We ___ a fortune for our new kitchen.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ a fortune for something
gaps.explanation: pay a fortune for something means to spend a very large amount buying it; the preposition 'for' follows 'pay'.

gaps.sentence: She ___ no difficulty finding the address.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ no difficulty doing something
gaps.explanation: have no difficulty (in) doing something is the fixed pattern; 'made no difficulty' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ attention when the teacher is speaking.
gaps.explanation: pay attention is the fixed collocation for listening or concentrating carefully.

gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.
